objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with epigastric discomfort and cramping pain.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Hi doctor—I've had cramping epigastric discomfort for about 2 hours, and it feels similar to episodes I’ve had before, usually after eating. I’ve also unintentionally lost some weight because I’ve been avoiding meals to prevent the pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any new swelling in my joints. My knee pain has been chronic, but nothing feels swollen or changed with these recent episodes.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual growths on your scalp?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual growths on my scalp. I mainly just feel the cramping discomfort in my upper abdomen after meals.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or discomfort in your skin lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Not really—no significant itching or new skin discomfort. It’s mainly just the cramping epigastric discomfort, mostly after I eat, and the recent weight loss from trying to avoid meals.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any trouble lifting your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I don’t have trouble lifting my arms above my head.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any loss of vision, and nothing like that has come with the episodes. It’s been strictly the cramping discomfort in my upper abdomen, mostly after eating.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a fever that’s been so high it feels like you’re burning up—something above 104°F (40°C) that makes you feel extremely hot or dizzy?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had a fever like that—I don’t feel burning hot, extremely dizzy, or anything above 104°F.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Not particularly—nothing unusually stressful or overwhelming. It’s mainly the cramping discomfort in my upper abdomen after meals, and I’ve been avoiding eating to keep the pain from coming on.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any burning or discomfort when you urinate?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any burning or discomfort when I urinate. It’s been limited to the cramping discomfort in my upper abdomen, mostly after I eat.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling chills lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t been feeling chills or having any feverish symptoms—just the cramping epigastric discomfort, mostly after meals. It’s been the same sort of pattern as my prior episodes.”
